skill.name: cold-email-nurture
skill.description: Design a 5-email nurture stream from a Pain Signal Profile + EVP. Each email has a subject, preheader, opener, body beats, CTA, cadence rationale, behavioral principle, and one route-to-sales trigger. Loaded by the main cold-email skill when the user asks to nurture, re-engage, or design a stream. Based on the JMC Lifecycle Nurture framework.
skill.summary: Create a structured five-email nurture stream with timing, messaging, and sales-routing triggers.
skill.author: cmj-hub

content.value_statement: Cold leads often need relevant follow-up instead of repeated sales asks. This skill turns audience pain signals and a value proposition into a timed five-email nurture stream with clear engagement triggers.
actual_capabilities: Designs a five-email nurture sequence from a Pain Signal Profile and value proposition.
Creates subjects, preheaders, openers, body beats, calls to action, and cadence rationales.
Adapts the sequence for no-reply, re-engagement, churned, and post-download contexts.
Applies insight, case study, reframe, soft close, and hard close stages.
Defines one route-to-sales behavior for each email.
limitations: It does not send emails or connect to an email service provider.
It does not verify contact consent, legal requirements, or deliverability.
It needs a clear audience pain profile and value proposition for relevant copy.
It documents sales triggers but does not configure webhooks, Slack, or SDR queues.

use_cases.title: Re-engage silent leads
use_cases.description: Build a measured follow-up stream for prospects who received an earlier message but did not reply.

use_cases.title: Reconnect with former customers
use_cases.description: Frame a five-touch sequence around what changed, what broke, and which improvements could earn another evaluation.

use_cases.title: Follow up after content downloads
use_cases.description: Turn a downloaded guide or report into helpful follow-up messages with permission-based next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic nurture stream
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a five-email no-reply nurture stream for [audience]. Use this pain signal profile: [profile]. Use this value proposition: [EVP]. Use a helpful, concise tone.

prompt_templates.title: Set the cadence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a five-email nurture stream for [audience] using send days [days]. Include a subject, preheader, opener, two body beats, binary call to action, cadence rationale, behavioral principle, and sales trigger for every email.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt for re-engagement
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt this nurture brief for a re-engagement campaign: [brief]. Use a curiosity-led first email, a permission-based soft close, and a clear final close. Keep each email tied to this pain signal profile: [profile].

prompt_templates.title: Build a complete campaign brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a five-email nurture stream for [audience] after [context]. Inputs: pain signal profile [profile], value proposition [EVP], cadence [days], and desired tone [tone]. Explain the behavioral principle, timing, and route-to-sales trigger for each email. Flag missing inputs before drafting.

output_examples.input: Audience: operations leaders. Pain signal: manual reporting delays decisions. Value proposition: automate weekly reporting. Context: no reply.
output_examples.output: Email 1, day 3: Subject: A faster weekly reporting check. Opener: Manual reporting can hide changes until the next review. CTA: Would a weekly reporting example help?

output_examples.input: Audience: former customers. Pain signal: onboarding friction caused churn. Value proposition: guided setup and clearer adoption milestones. Context: churned.
output_examples.output: Email 1, day 3: Subject: What changed after onboarding? Opener: I would value your view on where the setup experience fell short. CTA: What was the biggest obstacle?

output_examples.input: Audience: people who downloaded a planning guide. Pain signal: inconsistent quarterly planning. Value proposition: a repeatable planning workflow. Context: post-download.
output_examples.output: Email 5, day 40: Subject: Close the planning loop? CTA: Reply with walkthrough or close the loop. Sales trigger: An explicit request for a walkthrough.

best_practices: Tie every email to one audience pain signal and one clear message.
Use permission-based calls to action and respect the stated cadence.
Define one observable sales trigger for each email.
anti_patterns: Do not repeat the same pitch across all five emails.
Do not claim results, customer stories, or urgency without evidence.
Do not treat opens or clicks as consent to contact outside applicable rules.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a Pain Signal Profile, a value proposition, a nurture context, and an expected cadence.

faq.question: Which nurture contexts are supported?
faq.answer: It supports no reply, re-engagement, churned customers, and post-download follow-up contexts.

faq.question: How many emails does it create?
faq.answer: It creates a five-email stream with timing and a purpose for each touch.

faq.question: Does it send the emails?
faq.answer: No. It creates the messaging and documents downstream sales triggers.

faq.question: Can it define a sales handoff?
faq.answer: Yes. It defines one behavior per email that can route an engaged lead to sales.

faq.question: Does it handle compliance?
faq.answer: No. Review consent, regional requirements, suppression rules, and deliverability before sending.
